applicableAreas: southern property boundary where overhead electric lines are present
findings.comment: Proposed trees (Cedar Elm, Live Oak, Mexican Redbud, Texas Mountain Laurel) are shown on the landscape plan near overhead electric distribution lines, but the plant schedule does not document whether these species have utility-compatible (UC) status per ECM Appendix F. Without explicit UC designation, compliance with the 15-foot clearance requirement for non-utility-compatible trees cannot be verified.

applicableAreas: southern property boundary where overhead electric distribution lines are present
findings.comment: Cedar Elm and Live Oak are proposed near the overhead electric lines. The plant schedule does not document the mature height (per ECM Appendix F) for these species. Without explicit mature height specifications, it cannot be verified whether these trees meet the 40+ feet threshold that would trigger the 25-foot clearance requirement from distribution conductors.

applicableAreas: southeastern portion of the site near the property boundary
findings.comment: Measurement of the landscape plan shows a mitigation tree (M symbol) positioned only 9.2 feet from the utility pole on the southeastern property boundary. This violates the minimum 10-foot clearance requirement from overhead electric utility poles.

The landscape plan and plant schedule do not differentiate large trees (40+ feet mature height per ECM Appendix F) from smaller trees. Cedar Elm and Live Oak are proposed near overhead electric facilities but are not specifically marked or noted as large trees on the plans or in the schedule, preventing clear verification of whether they meet the 40+ foot threshold that triggers additional clearance requirements.

The landscape plan shows trees in proximity to overhead electric lines but does not provide any dimension lines, measurements, or notes verifying clearances from the outside conductor position. The grouping guidance specifies that conductors are offset laterally from pole centerlines by approximately 4+ feet, but no such analysis is documented on the plans.

applicableAreas: southern property boundary where trees are proposed near overhead electric facilities
findings.comment: Without documented UC status and mature height specifications for proposed trees, it cannot be definitively determined whether any trees are within prohibited clearance zones. No written approval from Austin Energy is visible in the submitted documents authorizing trees in any restricted zones, if such restrictions apply.
